predecessors.note: The page's infobox lists the Russian Empire as the predecessor and does not date the Empire's end; Cliopatria's Russian Empire row ends in 1916.

union.text: Kaliningrad Oblast, the former northern East Prussia
Sortavala and the Ladoga shore (Finnish until 1940; the gazetteer lacks the name)

land.text: Russia proper, the land the Bolsheviks claimed and took in November 1917-February 1918 (the RSFSR keyframe of 1917): without Kaliningrad, Tuva, the Kurils, southern Sakhalin, the Karelian Isthmus and Ladoga Karelia

successors.note: The page's infobox: 'Succeeded by Russian SFSR and Russian State'. The RSFSR dossier (another group) starts in November 1917 and carries those two Cliopatria years. fx-35 (1 Nov 2026): the land was Cliopatria's Russian Republic shape of 1918, which leaves about 9,000 cells of the Soviet heartland (Arkhangelsk, Vologda, Kirov, Tver, Saratov, Karelia, Samara-Syzran) to nobody at the end of 1917 and gives the RSFSR Tuva (618 cells, the independent Tuvan People's Republic) and Central Asian land; it is now the RSFSR keyframe of 1917 (Russia proper). October Revolution page: the Bolshevik-led attempts to gain power 'were largely successful in Russia proper' (Saratov 9 November 1917, Tver 10 November, Tsaritsyn 27 November, Petrozavodsk 17 January 1918, Vologda 8 February, Arkhangelsk 17 February) and 'less successful in ethnically non-Russian parts of the Empire'. The dissolve event's region stays the whole republic; the compiler reads the successors' land.

land.text: the page names the Russian State as a successor without a territory; its own dossier gives the land
the governorates the Central Rada claimed on 20 November 1917 (see the Ukrainian People's Republic dossier)

successors.note: The UPR page's infobox lists the Russian Republic as the UPR's predecessor and the UPR as 'autonomy within the Russian Republic (1917)'.

land.text: Transcaucasia, governed from Tiflis by the Transcaucasian Commissariat 'established at Tbilisi on 15 November 1917' and proclaimed the Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic on 22 April 1918: the region of that state's own 1918 keyframe

successors.note: Fix fx-40 (2 Nov 2026), window request R131. The Transcaucasian Commissariat page (opened 2 Nov 2026): 'The Transcaucasian Commissariat was established at Tbilisi on 15 November 1917', 'the first government of the independent Transcaucasia'; 'the TDFR was proclaimed as an independent state on 22 April 1918'. The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk page (opened 2 Nov 2026): 'Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Georgia rejected the treaty and instead declared independence' and 'Bolshevik control of Ukraine and Transcaucasia was, at the time, fragile or non-existent'. Without this entry the Georgian, Armenian and Azerbaijani cells (and Kars) of the republic went to nobody at its end. The state is born in April 1918; the compiler hands the land over at the end of 1917 because a successor may start in the year after the dissolution. The dossier of that state names this one as predecessor (its identity.predecessors[0]).

capitals.name: Petrograd (Saint Petersburg)
capitals.note: The infobox gives Petrograd as the only capital; the page does not mention the 1918 move to Moscow.

rulers.name: Alexander Kerensky
rulers.title: head of the Provisional Government
rulers.note: The page lists Kerensky as head of government from September to November 1917 and Georgy Lvov, who 'resigned in July 1917 in favor of his Minister of War', as his predecessor.

keyframe_review.note: 22.28 M km2 for 1917. The page gives no area (infobox area empty), so there is no ratio to take; its only territorial statement is that the republic claimed 'the territory of the former Russian Empire'. A gazetteer comparison (not a page) shows the shape is Cliopatria's Russian Empire 1916 shape without 424 cells of northern Iran and with 78 cells added near Romania. The shape runs to 31 December 1917 but the republic's government fell on 7 November, so the weeks from November belong to the RSFSR.

correction.text: Shape unchanged, but these years belong to Soviet Russia (russian-soviet-federative-socialist-republic), not to the Russian Republic, whose government was dissolved on 7 November 1917; after 3 March 1918 'Russia renounced all territorial claims in Finland' and 'Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, most of Belarus, and Ukraine'

keyframe_review.note: 17.85 M km2 (4.4 M km2 below 1917). The Brest-Litovsk page dates the loss (signed 17:50 on 3 March 1918; lands 'comprised 34% of the former empire's population, 54% of its industrial land') and fits the Finland, Ukraine, Belarus and Baltic cells that the shape drops. It does not explain the other cells the shape drops (Turkmenistan 1,254, Kazakhstan 706, Uzbekistan 491, Tajikistan 394): no page opened dates a loss of Turkestan, so a gap-filler or the RSFSR dossier must settle it.

correction.text: Shape unchanged, but this year belongs to Soviet Russia (russian-soviet-federative-socialist-republic), in the middle of the civil war: Red forces 'recaptured the city [Kazan] on 8 September 1918' and Ufa was 'retaken on 13 March' 1919

keyframe_review.note: 18.60 M km2 (+0.7 M km2 on 1918): the 2,876 added cells are Volga and Urals land (Russia 2,385, Kazakhstan 489), which fits the Red recapture of the Komuch and Directory lands dated on the Russian Civil War page. Not Russian-Republic land in any sense: the page's own text puts the republic's end in 1917.

region.text: the territory of the former Russian Empire

ledger.note: 1917, 14 September (1 September O.S.): Kerensky proclaims the Russian Republic. The page: proclaimed 'by the Russian Provisional Government on 1 September (14 September, N.S.) 1917 in a decree signed by Alexander Kerensky', after Kornilov's failed coup; it claimed 'the territory of the former Russian Empire'.

region.text: the whole republic: its land passes to Soviet Russia (the Bolshevik-held land) and, in the east, to the Russian State

ledger.note: 1917, 7 November: the Bolsheviks seize power and the republic's government is dissolved. The page: 'The government of the Russian Republic was dissolved after the Bolsheviks seized power by force on 7 November 1917.' The Constituent Assembly (elected 25 November) 'issued a decree' on 18 January 1918 and 'was dissolved by the Bolsheviks' the next day; the page dates the Russian Soviet Republic to 25 January 1918. Fix fx-40 (2 Nov 2026), R131: identity.successors gains the Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic (the Commissariat of 15 November 1917 and its successor), so Transcaucasia is no longer left to nobody. Not widened, for lack of a living successor dossier or of a page that places the land: Belarus (the Brest-Litovsk page has Russia lose 'most of Belarus' only in March 1918 and names no Belarusian state; no dossier for the Belarusian People's Republic exists, the Byelorussian SSR starts in 1919), Moldova/Bessarabia (the Russian Republic and Brest-Litovsk pages name no Moldavian state; no dossier), Lithuania and Courland ('already occupied by the Central Powers'), Estonia and Livonia ('The Baltic governorates were to become client states ruled by German princes'); the Russian Republic page itself says nothing on any of these regions.

wars.name: Eastern Front (World War I): Russian war effort to the armistice
wars.outcome: The armistice of 16 December 1917 at Brest-Litovsk and the treaty signed on 3 March 1918 ended the war on this front; the republic's government had already fallen on 7 November 1917.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered: 'On 16 December 1917 an armistice was signed between Russia and the Central Powers in Brest-Litovsk' (Russian Civil War page); the treaty's signing time is on the Brest-Litovsk page. Land lost by the treaty belongs to the RSFSR dossier.

wars.name: Russian Civil War
wars.outcome: The civil war opens on 7 November 1917, the day the republic's government falls; its territorial results are carried by the RSFSR, Russian State, South Russia and Far Eastern Republic dossiers.
wars.note: Infobox '7 November 1917 - 25 October 1922'. No zone is given here because no border of the Russian Republic itself moved in the war.

certainty.note: The republic claims the whole Russian Empire, whose treaty frontiers are sharp, but the western and Caucasian fronts were war lines and the page gives no boundary.

notes:
Pages: 3 (budget 1-2): the Russian Republic page is thin on land, so the Brest-Litovsk page explains the 1918 shape and the Russian Civil War page (opened anyway for the Ukrainian, Soviet-republics and Priamurye dossiers of this batch) explains 1919.

The state: the page treats the Russian Republic as the Provisional Government's republic of 1 (14) September to 7 November 1917; Cliopatria draws a 'Russian Republic' for 1917, 1918 and 1919. The 1918 and 1919 shapes are Soviet Russia's (RSFSR dossier, russian-soviet-federative-socialist-republic, which starts in November 1917 and names this row as predecessor); they are marked wrong here so the renderer takes the land from that dossier. The page also carries the republic's nominal end in the Constituent Assembly's dissolution (18-19 January 1918, with the Russian Soviet Republic proclaimed on 25 January 1918); the dossier ends at the government's fall on 7 November 1917.

Not settled: (1) the Central Asian cells missing from the 1918 shape (Turkestan) and the Caucasus: no page opened; (2) Finland's independence (December 1917, Russian Civil War page) and the Ukrainian Central Rada's Third Universal (20 November 1917, UPR page) fall in the weeks between the government's fall and New Year; they are in the Finland and UPR dossiers, not here; (3) the Russian Republic page gives no area. [Fix fx-40, 2 Nov 2026, R131] The successors list now also names transcaucasian-democratic-federative-republic (Transcaucasia). Belarus, the Baltic governorates and Moldova still go to nobody at the end of 1917: the pages opened (Russian Republic, Treaty of Brest-Litovsk, Transcaucasian Commissariat) place no state on that land before 1918 and the Belarusian People's Republic and Moldavian Democratic Republic have no dossier (handoffs in the fx-40 report). Turkestan is not widened: no page opened places a further state there in 1917 (dossiers exist for the russian-turkestan colony 1867-1918, the Alash Autonomy and the Bukhara and Khiva states, which name this republic or sit inside its shape), and the share of the 3,442 cells that go to nobody which lies in Turkestan is not known without a compile run.
